Metadata.title: {name} – Explore Your Amazing Body!
Metadata.description: A free, safe, interactive 3D human body explorer for learners aged 1 to 18, from toddlers to Class 11–12 BiPC and NEET students.
Metadata.exploreDescription: Spin, zoom and tap the 3D human body to discover what each part does, explained for your age.
Metadata.partTitle: {name}: what it is and what it does

tips.little: Tap the body and listen! Then tap Organs to find the heart.
tips.skin: Drag the peel slider to see what's under your skin!
tips.muscles: Muscles work in pairs. Find the biceps and the triceps!
tips.organs: Tap an organ, then try Close-up or Cut in half to look inside.
tips.skeleton: Can you find the longest bone? Hint: it's in your leg!
tips.circulatory: Red tubes carry blood away from the heart, blue tubes bring it back.
tips.nervous: Press 'Send a message' and watch it zoom to the hand!
tips.respiratory: Press 'Breathe with me' and breathe along with the lungs.
tips.digestive: Press 'Follow the food' to take a trip through your tummy!
tips.urinary: Your kidneys are near your back. Try the Back view!
tips.sensory: Tap a sense organ and try its experiment.
tips.immune: The spleen and thymus help train your body's defence team.
tips.endocrine: Hormones are chemical messages carried in your blood.
tips.selected: Tap 'Zoom into the tissue' to see what it's made of!
tips.tour: Not sure where to start? Take the body tour!

systemInfo.skeletal: Bones form the body's framework, protect organs such as the brain and heart, give muscles something to pull on, store calcium and make blood cells in the bone marrow.
systemInfo.muscular: Skeletal muscles are striated, voluntary muscles attached to bones by tendons. They work in antagonistic pairs to move joints, keep posture and produce heat.
systemInfo.cardiac: The heart is a four-chambered muscular pump. Its valves keep blood moving one way through the pulmonary and systemic circuits.
systemInfo.arterial: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. Their thick, elastic walls cope with high pressure; most carry oxygenated blood, except the pulmonary arteries.
systemInfo.venous: Veins bring blood back to the heart. They have thinner walls and valves that stop backflow; the pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood from the lungs.
systemInfo.nervous: The brain, spinal cord and nerves receive, process and send signals, controlling movement, sensation, thought and automatic body functions.
systemInfo.sensory: The eyes and ears contain receptors for sight, hearing and balance, with accessory structures such as the eyelids, tear apparatus and eye muscles.
systemInfo.respiratory: The respiratory system conducts air to the lungs, where oxygen enters and carbon dioxide leaves the blood across the alveoli.
systemInfo.digestive: The alimentary canal and its glands break food down, absorb nutrients and water, and remove undigested waste.
systemInfo.urinary: The kidneys filter blood to form urine, balancing water, salts and pH; urine flows through the ureters to the bladder and out through the urethra.
systemInfo.lymphatic: Lymphoid organs such as the thymus and spleen help lymphocytes mature and fight infection.
systemInfo.endocrine: Endocrine glands release hormones into the blood to coordinate growth, metabolism, stress responses and reproduction.
systemInfo.reproductive: The male reproductive system produces sperm and male sex hormones, and carries sperm to the outside.
systemInfo.integumentary: Hair grows from follicles in the skin and helps protect and insulate the body.
systemInfo.connective: Cartilage, ligaments, discs and membranes connect and cushion structures, stabilise joints and spread loads.
